blocks.text: INQUIRER.net / Updated as of: 07:58 AM November 16, 2026

MANILA, Philippines — With geopolitical tensions, regional security concerns and economic uncertainties looming over Southeast Asia, Manila becomes the center of high-level diplomacy as the Philippines hosts the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit and Related Summits from Nov. 15 to 18.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. leads the gathering, which brings together Southeast Asian leaders and dialogue partners, including the United States, China and Japan, for discussions on issues shaping the region’s future.
Among the key concerns are the crisis in Myanmar, tensions in the South China Sea, the economic fallout from the Middle East conflict and regional cooperation.
Follow our live updates for the latest developments, key statements, agreements and other developments from Manila./dp

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines will hand over the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) chairmanship without delivering the long-awaited Code of Conduct (COC) on the South China Sea, leaving Singapore to resolve contentious provisions despite Manila’s claim that negotiations on the proposed pact are 80 percent complete
